q.instruction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
q.passage: SENSIBLE SENTENCES? (From Week 8) Choose the word that makes sense in each of the sentences below. 1.Eric was (ⓐ<u>afflicted</u>, besieged) with an inoperable ailment. 2.The octogenarian refused to (ⓑ<u>succumb</u>, surge) to pneumonia. 3.The (ⓒ<u>remote</u>, ubiquitous) mayor was photographed in four different parts of the city yesterday. 4.We were worried lest the hostages be suffering from (sanctuary, ⓓ<u>nutrition</u>). 5.The (ⓔ<u>tranquil</u>, sinister) tone of the spring morning was suddenly broken by the loud explosion. 6.I heard his voice (excruciating, reverberating) through the corridors. 7.The senator’s bid for a second term was (thwarted, respited) by the electorate. 8.After the king’s death, his son (ascended, succumbed) to the throne in the normal order of succession. 9.The (privations, harbingers) that the poor people endured in their ghetto apartments were reprehensible. 10.The children were (emaciated, fretful) when awakened from their nap. 11.We were asked to (swap horses in midstream, cool our heels) while waiting for the bus.
q.explanation:
정답 ⓓ: 문맥상 'malnutrition'가 와야 하는데 'nutrition'가 쓰여 부적절하다 — 해당 문장 “We were worried lest the hostages be suffering from (sanctuary, malnutrition).”의 논리 흐름상 malnutrition 가 맞고 nutrition 는 방향이 어긋난다. [극성] correct=malnutrition (lack of nourishment) ↔ wrong=nutrition (adequate nourishment)
[오답 진단·처방]
① 진단: 학생은 'afflicted'를 골랐는데, 문장에서는 'besieged'가 더 자연스럽다. 'afflicted'는 질병을 가진 사람을 묘사하지만, 'besieged'는 압박받는 상황을 나타낸다. → 처방: 문맥에서 'besieged'가 적절한지 판단하려면, 'with an inoperable ailment'가 압박을 의미하는지 확인하고, 'afflicted'가 단순히 병에 걸린 상태만을 의미하므로 어울리지 않음을 인식하라.
② 진단: 학생은 'surge'를 골랐는데, 'succumb'가 맞다. 'surge'는 증가를 뜻해 문맥과 맞지 않는다. → 처방: 'succumb'가 'to pneumonia'와 함께 사용되는 일반적 표현인지 확인하고, 'surge'가 의미하는 '증가'와 문장 의미가 맞지 않음을 인지하라.
③ 진단: 학생은 'ubiquitous'를 골랐는데, 'remote'가 맞다. 'ubiquitous'는 어디에나 있는 것을 뜻해 문맥과 반대다. → 처방: 'remote'가 'mayor'와 함께 사용되는 상황인지, 'ubiquitous'가 반대 의미임을 기억하고, 문맥을 통해 적절한 단어를 선택하라.
⑤ 진단: 학생은 'sinister'를 골랐는데, 'tranquil'이 맞다. 'sinister'는 불길한 느낌을 주어 문맥과 맞지 않는다. → 처방: 문장 앞뒤를 보고 'tranquil'이 평온한 분위기를 묘사하는지, 'sinister'가 부정적 의미를 가지는지 판단하도록 연습하라.

q.passage: Confusing Words and Homonyms 27 consent (see assent) ⓐ<u>continual</u> repeated but with breaks in between; chronic Example: The continual ⓑ<u>problem</u> of our car not ⓒ<u>starting</u> ⓓ<u>allowed</u> us to ⓔ<u>sell</u> it. continuous without interruption in an unbroken stream of time or space Example: The continuous dripping of the faucet drove me crazy. core center or crucial part corps trained group corpse dead body cosign to sign along with cosine a trigonometry term council a group of people meeting for a purpose counsel (verb, noun) advise; advice, an attorney creak a sound creek a stream crews many groups cruise a trip or vacation by sea criteria plural of criterion criterion a standard for evaluating or testing something cue a hint; a stimulus queue a line of people waiting currant type of small berry current up to date curser someone who swears or wishes misfortune on another cursor a blinking symbol indicating position on a computer screen dam a barrier obstructing the ﬂow of liquid damn a swear word or curse dammed blocked from ﬂowing damned doomed
q.explanation:
정답 ⓓ: 문맥상 'forced'가 와야 하는데 'allowed'가 쓰여 부적절하다 — 해당 문장 “Confusing Words and Homonyms 27 consent (see assent) continual repeated but with breaks in between; chronic Example: The continual problem of our car ”의 논리 흐름상 forced 가 맞고 allowed 는 방향이 어긋난다. [극성] 정답=부정적 강제 ↔ 오답=긍정적 허용
[오답 진단·처방]
① 진단: 학생은 'continual' 낱말의 뜻을 정확히 이해하지 못했거나, 예문 속 낱말의 적절성 판단 기준을 혼동했습니다. → 처방: 낱말의 뜻을 정확히 파악하고, 예문이 그 낱말의 뜻을 설명하기 위해 쓰인 것임을 기억하며 문맥을 판단하세요.
② 진단: 학생은 'continual'의 뜻인 "반복되지만 중간에 끊김이 있는" 상황에 'problem'이 어울리지 않는다고 오해했습니다. → 처방: 'continual'이 '문제'와 결합하여 "계속 반복되는 문제"라는 자연스러운 뜻을 이룸을 이해하고 문맥을 다시 살피세요.
③ 진단: 학생은 'not starting'이 '차'와 '문제'라는 문맥에서 어색하다고 판단했거나, 'starting'의 동명사 쓰임을 혼동했습니다. → 처방: 'not starting'이 '시동이 걸리지 않는 것'이라는 뜻으로 '차의 문제점'을 정확히 나타냄을 파악하고 문맥을 다시 읽으세요.
⑤ 진단: 학생은 차의 'continual problem'이 'sell'이라는 행동으로 이어지는 것이 문맥상 부적절하다고 오해했습니다. → 처방: 'continual problem'으로 인해 차를 '파는' 것은 자연스러운 결과임을 이해하고, 문맥 속 인과 관계를 다시 생각하세요.

q.passage: Quick Quiz #22 Match each word in the first column with its definition in the second column. Check your answers here. 1. coalesce a. perceptive 2. coalition b. unite 3. coerce c. conversational 4. cogent d. force someone to do something 5. cognitive e. proportionate 6. cognizant f. making sense 7. coherent g. group with a purpose 8. colloquial h. powerfully convincing 9. collusion i. summary 10. commensurate j. forceful 11. compelling k. conspiracy 12. compendium l. dealing with how we know our environment COMPLACENT (kum PLAY sunt) adj self-satisfied; overly pleased with oneself; contented to a fault • The complacent camper paid no attention to the poison ivy around his campsite, and ended up going to the hospital. • The football team won so many games that it became complacent, and the worst team in the league won the game. To fall into complacency is to become ____.
q.explanation:
빈칸에는 'indifferent to one's environment'가 들어가 글의 논지를 완성한다 (본문 'comfortably uncaring about the world around you'의 패러프레이즈).
[오답 진단·처방]
① 진단: ‘deeply concerned with surroundings’는 ‘complacent’가 ‘자기 만족’이라는 뜻이라 ‘관심이 많다’와 반대임을 놓친다. → 처방: ‘complacent’는 ‘자기 만족’이라고 기억하고, ‘concern’과 반대임을 체크한다.
③ 진단: ‘aware of all things’를 ‘cognizant’와 혼동해 ‘complacent’와 비슷한 의미로 착각한다. → 처방: ‘complacent’는 ‘무관심’이며, ‘cognizant’는 ‘인지한’이므로 차이를 분명히 구분한다.
④ 진단: ‘mostly aware of surroundings’는 ‘complacent’보다 ‘conscious’에 가까운 표현으로, ‘indifferent’와 반대라는 점을 놓친다. → 처방: ‘indifferent’와 ‘aware’의 반의어 관계를 명확히 기억한다.
⑤ 진단: ‘eager to explore horizons’는 ‘adventurous’와 유사해 ‘complacent’와 상반된 뜻으로 착각한다. → 처방: ‘complacent’는 ‘자기 만족’이므로 ‘호기심’과 반대임을 재확인한다.

q.instruction: 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
q.passage: Quick Quiz #22 Match each word in the first column with its definition in the second column. Check your answers here. 1. coalesce a. perceptive 2. coalition b. unite 3. coerce c. conversational 4. cogent d. force someone to do something 5. cognitive e. proportionate 6. cognizant f. making sense 7. coherent g. group with a purpose 8. colloquial h. powerfully convincing 9. collusion i. summary 10. commensurate j. forceful 11. compelling k. conspiracy 12. compendium l. dealing with how we know our environment COMPLACENT (kum PLAY sunt) adj self-satisfied; overly pleased with oneself; contented to a fault • The complacent camper paid no attention to the poison ivy around his campsite, and ended up going to the hospital. • The football team won so many games that it became complacent, and the worst team in the league won the game. To fall into complacency is <u>to become comfortably uncaring about the world around you</u>.
choices: It means to become comfortably uncaring about the world around you.
It implies that excessive self‑satisfaction can blind one to looming dangers.
It suggests that you may grow indifferent to the emotions of others.
It means you will always be unconcerned about the world around you.
It indicates that feeling uncaring can make you more aware of potential threats.
q.explanation:
밑줄 친 부분은 'It implies that excessive self‑satisfaction can blind one to looming dangers.'을 함의한다.
[오답 진단·처방]
① 진단: 선지는 문장을 그대로 해석했으나, 'complacent'이 자기만족으로 위험을 눈감아버리는 뜻을 담고 있다는 점을 놓쳤다. → 처방: 단어의 정의와 문맥을 함께 살펴, 단순 번역보다 의미를 파악하도록 연습하라.
③ 진단: 선지는 'world around you'를 감정적 관계까지 확대해 해석했다. → 처방: 문맥에서 'world'가 물리적 환경인지, 감정적 관계인지 구분하도록 연습하라.
④ 진단: 'to become'을 현재형으로 해석해 항상 그렇다고 판단했다. → 처방: 동사의 시제와 의미를 구분해 변화 과정을 파악하도록 연습하라.
⑤ 진단: 'uncaring'이 경계심을 높인다고 잘못 해석했다. → 처방: 문장 구조를 따라가며 부정어와 결과를 정확히 파악하도록 연습하라.

q.passage: Lesson 5  Cohesion and Coherence 75 Here’s the point: Before you begin writing, name the things you are writing about. Those are your topics. They should be short, concrete, familiar words, and more often than not, they should name the main characters in your story. Most of your subjects should be topics. Most impor­ tant, be consistent: do not vary your subjects for the sake of variety. Your topics should tell your readers what a passage is globally “about.” Avoiding Distractions at the Beginning of a Sentence It is hard to begin a sentence well. Readers want to get to a ­subject/ topic quickly, but too often we begin sentences in ways that keep readers from getting there. It’s called throat-clearing. Throat-­ clearing typically begins with metadiscourse (review pp. 58–59) that connects a sentence to the previous one, with transitions such as and, but, therefore:

① Too uncertain: Some of my recent research seems to ­imply that there may be a risk that certain people with a gun in their homes could be more prone to use it to kill themselves or a ­family member than to protect themselves from ­possible intruders.
② ✓ Totalitarianism prevents stable social relationships.
③ My research indicates that people with a gun in their homes are more likely to use it to kill themselves or a family member than they are to protect themselves from an intruder.
④ Too certain: In my research, I prove that people with a gun in their home use it to kill themselves or a family member instead of to protect themselves from an intruder.
⑤ That’s little help, but this is a matter where you have to develop and then trust your ear.
